decisions.reason: The adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display remains very close to the firm's core POS display offering, though its lack of recent website visibility raises some risk of portfolio simplification.
The pegboard-back cardboard display is still a useful core variant for retail customers and fits the firm's established design and production strengths.
This standard cardboard quarter-pallet display overlaps strongly with other quarter-pallet formats, so in a narrow portfolio it is the most likely cardboard variant to be removed to free resources.
The eighth-pallet format serves different retail space requirements and therefore still supports the firm's one-stop display range despite some rationalisation risk.
The wooden display pallet is less central to a paper-based display specialist and is more likely to be discontinued as the firm concentrates on its core cardboard solutions and new development.
